REVENUE RECOGNITION MEMORANDUM
==============================================================================
Contract:            RL-2025-0633
Customer:            Cedar Point Wealth Advisors, LP
Prepared by:         Treatment Agent (Agent 3)
Reviewed by:         Audit Agent (Agent 4) - 18-item review checklist
Standard:            ASC 606, Revenue from Contracts with Customers
Recognition status:  Cleared for recognition; open items to be resolved before period close
==============================================================================

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE

   This memorandum documents the revenue recognition analysis for the
   arrangement identified above under ASC 606, Revenue from Contracts with
   Customers, and records the accounting conclusion, the recognition
   schedule, the journal entries, and the open items for follow-up.

2. FACTS AND CIRCUMSTANCES

   Cedar Point Wealth Advisors, LP has entered into a 12-month subscription
   contract with a total transaction price of $15,000. This amount comprises
   a fixed annual platform subscription fee of $12,000 and a one-time
   implementation service fee of $3,000. The contract includes standard
   support and updates as part of the subscription and contains no usage-
   based fees or discounts. The contract is valid and enforceable with
   defined terms, auto-renewal provisions, and no collectibility concerns.

3. AUTHORITATIVE GUIDANCE

   ASC 606-10-05-4               Revenue model — overview
   ASC 606-10-55-42 to 55-45     Customer options / material right; Material rights — discounted renewals/options
   ASC 606-10-25-14(b); 25-27    Subscription — single PO, ratable
   ASC 606-10-25-19 to 25-21; 55-51  Onboarding — non-distinct by default

   The paragraph references above point to the relevant provisions of ASC
   606; the entity's revenue policy paraphrases those provisions and should
   be read together with them.

4. ANALYSIS

   Identify the contract with the customer
      The Company has concluded that a valid, enforceable contract exists.
      We have concluded that a valid contract exists under ASC 606 as the
      agreement specifies the subscription term, fees, renewal terms at then-
      current list pricing, and enforceable termination provisions. There are no
      indications of unconstrained cancellation rights or collectibility issues,
      satisfying the criteria for contract identification.

   Identify the performance obligations
      1 performance obligation(s) were identified: core_subscription. On
      onboarding, onboarding is not distinct and is combined into the
      subscription.
      The contract contains a single performance obligation, which is the
      combined subscription service. The one-time implementation service is not
      distinct because access to the platform is conditioned on completion of
      implementation, and the implementation is integrated with the subscription
      service. Therefore, the implementation service is combined with the
      subscription into one performance obligation.

   Determine the transaction price
      The transaction price is $15,000.00. The arrangement includes no variable
      consideration and no discount.
      The transaction price is fixed at $15,000, consisting of the $12,000
      annual subscription fee and the $3,000 implementation fee. There are no
      variable consideration components, discounts, or material rights affecting
      the transaction price. Renewal pricing is at then-current list prices and
      does not confer a material right.

   Allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations
      A single performance obligation was identified; no allocation is required.
      Since there is only one combined performance obligation, the entire
      transaction price of $15,000 is allocated to that single obligation. No
      allocation among multiple obligations is necessary.

   Recognise revenue as performance obligations are satisfied
      Revenue is recognised ratably over time over 12 months.
      Revenue is recognised over time on a ratable basis over the 12-month
      contract term. This reflects the continuous transfer of control of the
      subscription service to the customer throughout the period. The
      implementation service is included in this pattern of recognition as it is
      not distinct.

   Revenue is recognised on a straight-line monthly basis. Partial first or

6. JOURNAL ENTRIES

   On invoice

          Cr  2400 Deferred Revenue - Current              $15,000.00
      Record the contract liability on billing in advance of performance.

      Dr  2400 Deferred Revenue - Current                   $1,250.00
          Cr  4100 Subscription Revenue                     $1,250.00
      Release the contract liability as the subscription is delivered.

7. OPEN ITEMS AND MATTERS FOR FOLLOW-UP

   [MEDIUM] Bundled onboarding distinctness
      Facts and circumstances:  separately priced onboarding fee of 3000.0 alongside subscription of 12000.0
      Question:                 Is the onboarding customized to the customer and required before the customer can access the platform (suggesting it is not distinct and should be combined), or is it standardized, optional, and available elsewhere (suggesting a separate performance obligation)? Confirm whether the onboarding fee is being front-loaded rather than recognized over the service period.
      Recommended procedure:    Document whether the onboarding is customised and required for platform access (combine into the subscription obligation) or standardised and optional (separate obligation). Retain the evidence relied on.
      Timing:                   Before period close
      Disposition:              open
      The separately priced onboarding fee of $3,000 alongside the $12,000
      subscription fee warrants documentation of whether the onboarding is
      customised and required for platform access, which supports combining it
      into the subscription performance obligation, or if it is standardised and
      optional, which would support treating it as a separate obligation.
      Evidence relied upon for this conclusion should be retained.

8. MATTERS CONSIDERED AND CONCLUDED IMMATERIAL

   No quantified matter was concluded immaterial on this contract.

9. COMPLETENESS OF REVIEW

   The 18-item review checklist was completed in full. Of the 18 matters, 1
   is reported at section 7, 0 at section 8, and 17 were considered and
   concluded not applicable to this contract on the facts. The completed
   checklist, with the basis for each conclusion, is retained in the
   structured review record.

10. CONCLUSION

   In summary, the contract with Cedar Point Wealth Advisors, LP represents a
   single performance obligation comprising the subscription service and the
   implementation service combined. The fixed transaction price of $15,000 is
   allocated entirely to this obligation. Revenue is recognised ratably over
   the 12-month term, consistent with the continuous transfer of control.
   There are no variable consideration elements, discounts, or material
   rights impacting the accounting. The contract is valid and enforceable
   under ASC 606, and the revenue recognition approach aligns with the
   guidance and relevant policies.

   Recognition status: Cleared for recognition; open items to be resolved before period close

   Scope and limitations: allocation of the transaction price across
   performance obligations by relative standalone selling price is not
   implemented; partial periods are not prorated by days; variable
   consideration is excluded from the transaction price and recognised as
   incurred.

metadata.text: In evaluating whether a promise is separately identifiable, the objective is to determine whether the entity is transferring each good or service individually or, instead, a combined item to which the individual goods or services are inputs. Factors indicating that two or more promises are not separately identifiable include: the entity provides a significant service of integrating the goods or services into a combined output; one or more of the goods or services significantly modifies or customizes another; or the goods or services are highly interdependent or highly interrelated. Implementation, configuration, data-migration, or setup activities that an entity must complete before the customer can access or operate the underlying service typically indicate the promises are not separately identifiable and are therefore combined into a single performance obligation.

audit_findings.review_question: Has the variable portion been identified and separated from any fixed fee? Is RevLens recognizing usage as it is invoiced/incurred (right-to-invoice), or does the arrangement require estimating variable consideration? Confirm the fixed portion's recognition is not inflated by unearned usage.

audit_findings.name: minimum_commitment_floor
audit_findings.risk: Committed minimum and above-floor usage may be conflated.
audit_findings.review_question: Is the committed minimum being recognized as fixed consideration over the term, with only usage above the included volume treated as variable? Confirm the minimum is recognized regardless of actual usage.

audit_findings.name: unestimable_or_volatile_usage
audit_findings.risk: Variable consideration may be over-recognized where it cannot be reliably estimated.
audit_findings.review_question: Has the variable consideration estimate been constrained to the amount highly probable not to reverse? Where usage is seasonal or unpredictable, is revenue recognized only as the usage occurs rather than estimated for the full term?

audit_findings.name: usage_royalty_vs_ordinary_usage
audit_findings.risk: A fee tied to a license of IP may be mis-classified as ordinary usage (or vice versa).
audit_findings.review_question: Is the variable fee consideration for a license of RevLens intellectual property (apply the royalty exception), an ordinary metered usage fee (variable consideration), or the purchase of new capacity the customer did not previously control (a separate option/purchase)? Confirm the correct one.

audit_findings.name: discount_allocation_method
audit_findings.risk: A bundle discount may be allocated to the wrong obligations.
audit_findings.review_question: Is the discount allocated proportionately across all performance obligations by default? A discount is directed to a specific obligation only where RevLens regularly sells each item separately and regularly sells the discounted item on its own at a comparable discount — is that evidence present?

audit_findings.name: ssp_not_observable_residual
audit_findings.risk: Allocation may be unreliable where a standalone selling price is not observable.
audit_findings.review_question: Is at least one component supported by an observable standalone selling price, and is the residual approach applied only to the component whose price is genuinely not observable? Confirm the allocation is not based on an unsupported SSP estimate.

audit_findings.name: multiple_performance_obligations
audit_findings.risk: Allocation and recognition errors increase with the number of POs.
audit_findings.review_question: Has the transaction price been allocated across all obligations by relative SSP, and is each obligation recognized on its correct pattern (over time for the subscription; at completion for distinct one-time deliverables; by effort/hours for professional services)?

audit_findings.name: material_right_renewal_or_fee
audit_findings.risk: A discounted renewal or nonrefundable upfront fee may hide a separate performance obligation.
audit_findings.review_question: Does the renewal/option price sit significantly below the price offered to comparable customers (a material right), requiring a portion of the transaction price to be allocated to it and recognized at exercise or expiry? For an upfront fee waived on renewal, has the material-right question been assessed?

audit_findings.name: billing_timing_balances
audit_findings.risk: Deferred revenue vs contract asset may be mis-stated based on billing timing.
audit_findings.review_question: Where the customer is billed in advance, is a contract liability (deferred revenue) recorded and released as performance occurs? Where RevLens performs before it can bill (e.g., monthly in arrears), is a contract asset recorded rather than deferred revenue?

audit_findings.name: proration_partial_period
audit_findings.risk: Partial first/last periods may be recognized as full months.
audit_findings.review_question: Is the partial first or last month prorated by days, with full amounts only for complete months? Confirm proration changes only the timing pattern, not the total transaction price.

audit_findings.name: financing_component_check
audit_findings.risk: A significant financing component may exist on long-dated prepayments.
audit_findings.review_question: Has a significant financing component been considered for the multi-year prepayment, and is the conclusion (typically immaterial) documented? Confirm the practical expedient for one-year-or-less arrangements is not being misapplied to a multi-year prepayment.

audit_findings.name: free_or_promotional_period
audit_findings.risk: Free promotional periods may be recognized as zero-revenue rather than spread.
audit_findings.review_question: Is the total transaction price spread over the entire access period including the free portion (a lower monthly rate), rather than treating the free months as periods of zero revenue?

audit_findings.name: contract_validity_collectibility
audit_findings.risk: Revenue may be recognized on an arrangement that is not a valid, collectible contract.
audit_findings.review_question: Are the Step 1 criteria met — approval, identifiable rights and payment terms, commercial substance, and probable collection of substantially all consideration? If not, recognition should be withheld and the arrangement escalated.

audit_findings.name: missing_service_period_or_dates
audit_findings.risk: Recognition timing cannot be established without a defined service period or start.
audit_findings.review_question: Can the recognition period and start date be determined from the contract? If the term or go-live is unspecified, a recognition schedule should not be produced; the missing term should be flagged and obtained.

audit_findings.name: undetermined_distinctness_or_po_count
audit_findings.risk: The number of performance obligations cannot be concluded from the facts given.
audit_findings.review_question: Are the facts sufficient to apply the distinct criteria and the separability factors? If not, the PO count should not be fixed; the specific missing facts (customization, dependency, third-party availability) should be flagged as open questions.

audit_findings.name: silent_renewal_materiality
audit_findings.risk: A possible material right may be missed where renewal pricing is unstated.
audit_findings.review_question: Is the renewal price specified, and is it at, above, or below the price offered to comparable customers? Without this, whether the option conveys a material right cannot be concluded and should be flagged.
